name: list_processes
summary: List running processes ranked by CPU or memory. Each row: PID, Apple/system vs user app, %CPU, %MEM, owner, run time, command. Answers 'what's eating my CPU/memory/battery' and 'is anything stuck'.

params.name: sort_by
params.description: Rank by 'cpu' (default) or 'memory' (largest resident footprint first).

params.name: filter
params.description: Case-insensitive substring; only matching commands/names are shown (e.g. 'chrome'). Matched locally, never via a shell.

params.name: scope
params.description: 'all' (default) or 'user' (only the current login user's processes).

name: process_info
summary: Show everything about one process by PID: full command line, executable path, parent, owner, %CPU/%MEM, start time and run length, state (incl. zombie/defunct), Apple/system vs user app, and whether launchd auto-starts it. Use list_processes to find the PID.

params.name: pid
params.description: Process ID to inspect (from list_processes). Must be > 1.

name: cpu_load
summary: Report overall CPU pressure: 1/5/15-min load averages raw and per-core (~1.0 per core = fully busy), core count, and the top CPU processes. Judges whether the whole machine is overloaded, not just one app.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many top CPU processes to include (1–20, default 5).

name: memory_stats
summary: Report system memory: total RAM, used vs free, and the wired/active/inactive/compressed breakdown, plus the top memory processes. Judges memory pressure and what holds the most RAM.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many top memory processes to include (1–20, default 5).

name: gpu_stats
summary: Report built-in GPU utilization: overall device %, renderer and tiler %, and GPU memory in use. Per-process GPU isn't available without admin rights, so this is whole-device; check GPU-helper processes (WindowServer, *.WebKit.GPU) in list_processes to guess the driver.

name: startup_items
summary: List programs that auto-start via macOS launchd (background agents/daemons), with each one's label, current PID if running, and last exit status. Defaults to third-party — 'what did I install that auto-starts'. Classic Login Items aren't included (they need an Automation grant).

params.name: scope
params.description: 'third_party' (default, hides Apple's com.apple.* items) or 'all' (every launchd item).

params.name: limit
params.description: How many items to show (1–200, default 50).

name: top_processes
summary: Show a live, real-time snapshot of the busiest processes from `top` — instantaneous %CPU and memory per process, right now. Use this over list_processes when you want the current moment's CPU pressure (list_processes reports ps's averaged %CPU, which lags); use list_processes for richer per-process detail, filtering, and origin (Apple vs user app).

params.name: sort_by
params.description: Rank by 'cpu' (default, live %CPU) or 'memory' (largest footprint first).

params.name: limit
params.description: How many processes to show (1–50, default 15).

name: quit_process
summary: Gracefully quit the GUI app that owns a PID via the normal Quit command, so it can prompt to save. STAGED; can lose unsaved work and is not undoable. GUI apps only — use terminate_process for background/daemon processes. Never force-kills.

params.name: pid
params.description: Process ID of the GUI app to quit (from list_processes). Must be > 1.

name: terminate_process
summary: Ask a background/daemon process to exit via SIGTERM (the polite 'please shut down' signal), letting it clean up first. STAGED; not undoable. Never sends SIGKILL (force kill). GUI apps are refused — use quit_process so they can prompt to save.

params.name: pid
params.description: Process ID to send SIGTERM to (from list_processes). Must be > 1 (PID 1 and below are protected).
